action: Install the November 2026 Microsoft updates, starting with Outlook (CVE-2026-124194, exploited) and the 9.8-rated Windows LDAP, Windows Search and Xbox Live Networking flaws. Tell users not to open unexpected message-file attachments.
exec: A very large update with one actively exploited email flaw; prompt patching of Outlook and Windows reduces credential-theft risk.
plain: Microsoft's monthly security update fixes 1,093 flaws. One in Outlook is already being used by attackers: opening a specially made email can leak a scrambled form of the user's password. A serious Windows Search flaw is also fixed.

key_findings: MSRC's November 2026 Security Updates release was first published November 10 and last revised November 17.
As of November 17 the Security Update Guide lists 1,098 Microsoft-issued CVEs under the release, including items added after release day, and 64 rated Critical.
Only one is marked exploited: CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook spoofing flaw (6.5) that leaks the user's NTLMv2 hash when a crafted message file is opened; it was not publicly disclosed.
Critical flaws scored 9.8 include Windows LDAP (CVE-2026-119958), Windows Search (CVE-2026-116928), Xbox Live Networking Service (CVE-2026-112967), Azure OpenAI and Azure Managed Grafana.
For the Outlook flaw the Preview Pane is not an attack vector and MSRC lists no mitigation or workaround.
recommendations: Install the November 10 security update for every affected Outlook version; Microsoft lists no workaround.
Tell users not to open unexpected message files sent as attachments, since opening is the trigger.
Apply the updates for the Critical 9.8 remote code execution flaws in Windows LDAP, Windows Search and Xbox Live Networking Service.

summary: The second four-digit release in a row includes 63 critical flaws. CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook spoofing bug that leaks NTLMv2 hashes when a crafted message is opened, is under active attack. Analysts also flag a Windows Search remote code execution bug rated 9.8.
title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday: 1,093 fixes and an exploited Outlook zero-day

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) document: the Security Update Guide data for release 2026-Nov. The release-notes page and full CVRF file did not load. MSRC's current totals (1,098 CVEs, 64 Critical) include post-release additions; the release-day figures of 1,093 and 63 come from news coverage.
